themes: Shift from Transaction to Recurring Revenue
key_points: MOFSL transitioning to AUM-led, annuity-driven model with 21% AUM CAGR (FY26-29E) driving 19% revenue CAGR
Strong operating leverage expected with 22% operating profit CAGR (FY26-29E) outpacing revenue growth through cost moderation and RM productivity gains
Mix shift towards higher-margin AMC (23% AUM CAGR) and Private Wealth (25% AUM CAGR) will increase annuity revenues from 34.4% (FY26) to 41% (FY30E)
Indian mutual funds AUM projected to grow 18% CAGR (FY26-30E) with HNI wealth and alternatives growing 20%+ CAGR, supporting structural tailwinds
Market share gains across segments: equity ADTO share at 8.6% (FY26), SIP market share expanded to 4.7%, positioning for retail financialisation benefits
SOTP valuation of Rs1,150 implies 19x FY27E PE with higher multiples for asset-light businesses (AMC 28x, Private Wealth 25x) versus capital markets 14x
catalysts: AUM expansion execution across wealth and alternatives segments
Operating leverage realization and margin expansion
Private Wealth Management and AMC revenue mix improvement
HNI and UHNI client acquisition and retention
SIP flow acceleration and market share gains
reports.summary: UBS initiates Motilal Oswal Financial Services at Buy with Rs1,150 price target, viewing the company as a structural beneficiary of India's financialisation wave and its transition to an AUM-led, annuity-driven platform. Strong operating leverage with 22% earnings CAGR (FY26-29E) driven by 21% AUM expansion and improving business mix towards higher-margin wealth and asset management segments. Current valuation of 15x forward PE offers attractive entry point given the shift to recurring, less cyclical revenue streams.
reports.connection_narrative: India is experiencing a structural shift in household savings towards market-linked financial assets, with mutual fund AUM penetration well below global benchmarks and projected to grow at 18% CAGR through FY30E. This financialisation megatrend is reinforced by rising demat accounts, increasing retail participation through SIPs, and strong demand for professionally managed products among high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth segments. Motilal Oswal Financial Services is uniquely positioned to capitalize on this transformation through its diversified platform spanning wealth management, asset management, and alternatives. The company is executing a deliberate strategic transition from transaction-driven broking revenues toward a recurring, AUM-linked earnings model where growth becomes increasingly non-linear as platform investments scale. Within this evolution, MOFSL benefits from its 8.6% equity market share, expanding SIP market share at 4.7%, and strong distribution network that enables cross-selling across retail and HNI segments. The business model exhibits superior operating leverage with operating profit expected to grow at 22% CAGR (FY26-29E) ahead of revenue growth at 19%, driven by moderating costs as existing infrastructure scales and relationship manager productivity improves. The most critical catalyst to watch is the successful execution of the AUM CAGR target of 21% across all segments, particularly the acceleration of Private Wealth Management and alternative asset growth which should drive the annuity revenue share from 34% to 41% by FY30E, fundamentally re-rating the business quality toward premium wealth management multiples. The primary risk is if market volatility or changes in investor sentiment disrupt SIP momentum or high-net-worth inflows, potentially impacting the AUM growth assumptions that underpin the entire valuation thesis.
